propositions: Python 3.11 asyncio.wait_for consumes external cancellation when child future completes in same turn, causing worker to loop with cancelling()==1 while lifespan awaits indefinitely, triggering CI hang guard timeout.

Opcert worker in app.py:76-85 wrapped asyncio.to_thread(jobs.run_job) in asyncio.wait_for, which on Python 3.11 can swallow shutdown cancellation colliding with job completion, violating bounded queue/shutdown contract.

TestClient teardown hangs after test_matching_guard_is_accepted on Python 3.11 because worker does not terminate promptly when cancellation races with job completion, but Python 3.12+ passes due to asyncio.timeout semantics.
Fix replaces asyncio.wait_for with asyncio.timeout context manager in app.py:76-83 to preserve external cancellation and match Python 3.12 behavior while retaining per-job timeout guarantee.

Regression test oracle test_worker_cancellation_survives_job_completion_race observed RED before fix and GREEN after on Python 3.11, and mutation restoring wait_for returns it to RED, confirming defect and fix.
Accepted-job semantics, terminal record schema, one-worker queue, per-job timeout, and Python 3.12+ behavior remain unchanged; no API, config, or caller contract affected.
